subject: Career
title: What Recruiters Actually Look For
description: One-minute skill: What Recruiters Actually Look For.

hook.text: You think recruiters care about your skills section. They mostly skip it.

buildup.text: A LinkedIn survey found recruiters prioritize job titles, company names, and tenure.

discovery.text: They're pattern-matching: does this person's trajectory fit the role?

twist.text: Skills lists feel productive to write but rarely differentiate. Everyone claims teamwork.

climax.text: What stands out is evidence: numbers, outcomes, promotions. Proof beats claims.

punchline.text: Don't list skills. Show what you did with them.

quiz.question: What do recruiters prioritize when scanning resumes?

details.summary: Recruiters look for pattern matches between the role requirements and your resume, assessing career progression, relevant keywords, quantified impact, and cultural signals, all within seconds. Understanding their evaluative framework lets you structure your resume to match their scanning pattern.
details.whyItMatters: Most resumes are written from the applicant's perspective. Rewriting from the recruiter's perspective ensures your most relevant qualifications are positioned where reviewers actually look.
takeaways: Recruiters scan for role-relevant keywords before reading full content
Career progression and tenure patterns tell the recruiter about reliability
Quantified achievements catch attention more than responsibility lists

faq.question: What is the biggest red flag recruiters look for when scanning resumes?
faq.answer: Frequent job changes without clear progression is the most common red flag. Multiple roles lasting less than one year suggests either poor hiring decisions or a pattern of disengagement. If your history includes short tenures, address the reasons proactively in your cover letter.

faq.question: How do recruiters decide which resumes to recommend to hiring managers?
faq.answer: Recruiters create shortlists by matching resumes to a checklist of must-have and nice-to-have criteria from the job description. They then evaluate career trajectory, communication quality, and cultural fit signals. Making it easy for them to check off requirements increases your chances.
